Definition: from a derivative of πόρος (a way, i.e. means); furnishing (procuring), i.e. (by implication) money-getting (acquisition):--gain.
BiblicalUsage: Porismos means gain, money-getting, and Paul uses it twice in one warning. Some suppose that gain is godliness, and he answers that godliness with contentment is great gain.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the world has the equation backwards, and contentment is the only gain that cannot be taken away.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
